ai.title: Gravity Index link references resolved to tracked click URLs
ai.summary: The render_ui tool now accepts a Gravity Index link reference object (a source of gravity_index plus search_id and service_slug) in place of a raw http(s) URL, and the agent runtime resolves it to the exact tracked click URL stored in a prior gravity_index result before streaming the tool call to any client. This prevents the agent from transcribing or guessing opaque vendor URLs, so the rendered signup button points at the advertiser-tracked click URL byte-for-byte. The gravity-index tool description and render-ui schema were updated together so the agent is instructed to pass the reference rather than the URL.
ai.evidence: New file `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/gravity-index-cta.ts` exports `resolveGravityIndexLink`; `packages/agent-runtime/src/tools/tool-executor.ts` imports and calls it inside the `render_ui` branch when `widget.link` is a non-string object, replacing the reference with the resolved click URL before the `tool_call` event and before the handler runs. `common/src/tools/params/tool/render-ui.ts` adds the `gravityIndexButtonLinkSchema` (a `RenderUIGravityIndexLink` object) to the `link` union and exports `RenderUIGravityIndexLink`; `common/src/tools/params/tool/gravity-index.ts` updates the setup-link description to tell the agent to pass a Gravity reference to `render_ui` rather than the opaque URL.
ai.unknowns: The rollout and whether the same resolver is reused by other tool consumers is not shown in this commit.

changes.what: Resolves a Gravity Index link reference to the exact tracked click URL before streaming render_ui calls; the resolver fails closed for unknown searches, services, or unsafe URLs.
Adds the gravityIndexButtonLinkSchema to the render_ui widget link union and exposes the RenderUIGravityIndexLink type.
Updates the gravity_index tool description to instruct calling render_ui with a Gravity reference containing the exact search_id and service_slug instead of the opaque URL.

facts: Cap on the weekly GLM streak bonus: at most this many 7-day tiers count, so a 28-day (or longer) streak earns 4 GLM sessions per week.
Below the milestone this is the first tier being unlocked (1/week); at 7+ it's whatever tier the current streak has earned (up to 4/week).

Weekly GLM sessions earned by a streak of `streak` days, ignoring the feature gates: one per completed 7-day interval, capped at `FREEBUFF_STREAK_GLM_BONUS_MAX_MULTIPLIER` (a 28-day streak earns the max).

Resolve the live GLM weekly bonus directly from usage dates. The weekly pool gets +1 per completed 7 days of the current streak (7 → 1/week, 14 → 2/week, capped at 4 for 28+) and therefore refills every Monday Pacific; once the streak breaks it gets 0.

ai.title: Weekly GLM streak bonus scales with streak length
ai.summary: Weekly GLM streak bonus now scales with streak length. New `getFreebuffStreakGlmWeeklyUnits` calculates tiers based on completed 7-day intervals, capped by `FREEBUFF_STREAK_GLM_BONUS_MAX_MULTIPLIER` (4). eli5.text: If you keep coming back to Chatbase day after day, your weekly GLM credit bonus now grows the longer your streak gets. After a full week of daily visits you earn one extra GLM session each week, two after two weeks, three after three, and it tops out at four extra sessions per week once your streak hits 28 days. The bonus only applies to full-access users and resets every Monday, and if you miss a day your weekly GLM bonus drops back to zero until you rebuild your streak.

ai.title: Add raw HTTP diagnostics to startAgentRun failures
ai.summary: Added `console.error` calls in `startAgentRun` to log raw HTTP status, body, and error objects alongside the existing `logger` calls. This prevents silent failure drops caused by unallowlisted events in the web logger, ensuring opaque "Failed to start agent run" errors include diagnosable context. Scope limited to `sdk/src/impl/database.ts`. Response body text is truncated to 2000 characters.

eli5.text: When starting an agent run fails, you previously might have seen a vague "Failed to start agent run" message with no details, especially if your error logging tool silently dropped certain error types. The system now also prints the raw HTTP status, status text, and response body (truncated to 2000 characters) directly to your console alongside the existing logs, so you can see what the server actually returned or what went wrong during the request. This change is live today and applies whenever an agent run start request fails or returns unexpected data, making previously opaque failures diagnosable without needing to inspect code or logs manually.

facts: Run context-pruner before each step. cacheExpiryMs is baked to 30 minutes: the 5-minute default forces a full lossy re-summarization after any short idle even when the context is nowhere near its limit.
Run-id prefix for runs that skip the run-tracking ledger (context-pruner). These ids exist only in-process and must never be sent to the web API.

Always count locally. The token-count web API round-trip (full history + tools shipped to the server, which relays to Anthropic) added seconds of serial overhead to every step; there is no paid mode anymore that needs Anthropic-exact counts, and context-limit checks only need an estimate.
Untracked runs (context-pruner) have no ledger row, so their ids must not be reported as children on the parent's tracked steps.

ai.title: Context pruner skips run ledger and uses local token counting
ai.summary: Context-pruner runs now bypass the run-tracking ledger, minting local `untracked-` prefixed IDs to eliminate three web-API round-trips per step. Token counting switched to local estimation, removing serial latency from Anthropic API relays as exact counts are no longer required for free-mode limits. `cacheExpiryMs` baked to 30 minutes in `base2.ts`, `base-deep.ts`, and `general-agent.ts` to prevent lossy re-summarization after short idles. Untracked child run IDs are filtered out in `spawn-agent-utils.ts` to prevent reporting to parent steps.

eli5.text: Every few seconds your assistant trims its own memory before taking the next step, and it now counts words locally instead of asking a server each time, so steps keep moving without waiting on a network call. The trim job also keeps cached content for 30 minutes (instead of 5) before rewriting summaries, which stops it from re-summarizing after short pauses. Because the trim job skips the usual tracking ledger, it uses short-lived IDs that are never reported back to the parent run, so it doesn't pollute your run history. If you're running the assistant today, you'll notice steps keep flowing sooner after each question rather than hitting a small network pause.

facts: Jitters the adaptive healthy cadence and exponentially backs off failures so a shared outage cannot synchronize every CLI into a fixed retry wave.
entries.title: CLI update: use-connection-status
entries.summary: New files: `cli/src/utils/polling-backoff.ts`.

ai.title: Shared polling backoff replaces fixed-interval retries in CLI
ai.summary: A new `cli/src/utils/polling-backoff.ts` module centralizes the CLI's retry and cadence logic, exporting `failedPollDelayMs` and `jitterPollIntervalMs` which add equal-jitter exponential backoff (`FAILURE_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 20_000`, `FAILURE_BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 300_000`) to failed polls and jitter to healthy polling intervals. `useConnectionStatus` now calls `scheduleFailedCheck` plus `failedPollDelayMs`/`jitterPollIntervalMs` instead of resetting a fixed `INITIAL_INTERVAL`, and `useFreebuffSession` feeds `retryAfterMs` (parsed from `response.headers.get('retry-after')` by the new `parseRetryAfterMs`) into `failedPollDelayMs` via the `FreebuffSessionRequestError` type. This removes the hardcoded `POLL_INTERVAL_ERROR_MS = 10_000` path so a shared backend outage no longer synchronizes every CLI into a fixed retry wave.
ai.evidence: New file `cli/src/utils/polling-backoff.ts` defines `failedPollDelayMs`, `jitterPollIntervalMs`, `FAILURE_BACKOFF_BASE_MS = 20_000`, `FAILURE_BACKOFF_MAX_MS = 300_000`, and `RandomSource`; both `useConnectionStatus` and `useFreebuffSession` now import and call these helpers instead of the old fixed-error interval, and `FreebuffSessionRequestError` plus `parseRetryAfterMs` were added to `cli/src/utils/freebuff-session-api.ts` and consumed in `callFreebuffSession`'s error throw and the session hook's catch path.
